healthInfo.healthcareSystem: Universal (National Health Insurance / 국민건강보험 — mandatory for residents)
healthInfo.qualityNotes: Excellent healthcare system with world-class hospitals and advanced technology. English is available at larger hospitals in Seoul and Busan but limited elsewhere. Healthcare is affordable by Western standards. National Health Insurance does NOT cover tourists — you pay out-of-pocket or through travel insurance.
healthInfo.pharmacyHours: Most pharmacies (약국) open 9am-9pm. Some are open 24/7 in larger cities. Look for the green '약' sign. Some medications are available only at hospitals, not regular pharmacies.
healthInfo.pharmacyTips: Pharmacies are widely available. Many medications require a prescription. Some common medications are available OTC. Prescription medications must be dispensed at a pharmacy with a valid Korean prescription. Hospital prescriptions can be filled at external pharmacies.
healthInfo.prescriptionRules: Most medications require a Korean doctor's prescription. Foreign prescriptions are NOT accepted. You must see a Korean doctor to get a prescription. Some controlled substances require special permits.

restrictedMeds.name: Pseudoephedrine (Sudafed and similar)
restrictedMeds.note: Medications containing pseudoephedrine are prohibited. Sudafed, Contac, and similar products cannot be brought into South Korea.

restrictedMeds.name: Adderall/amphetamines (ADHD medications)
restrictedMeds.note: Strictly prohibited. ADHD medications containing amphetamines or methylphenidate (Adderall, Ritalin, Vyvanse, Concerta) are illegal to bring into South Korea.

restrictedMeds.name: Codeine-containing medications
restrictedMeds.note: Codeine is controlled. A prescription is required.

restrictedMeds.name: Medical cannabis
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal in South Korea with severe penalties.

healthInfo.bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all medications with generic names. Bring sufficient supply in original packaging. For any potentially problematic medications, contact the Korean embassy before travel. Controlled medications require a permit from KDF (Korea Drug & Food International).

travelInsurance.requiredNote: Not legally required but essential — healthcare costs can add up quickly without coverage.
travelInsurance.tips: National Health Insurance does not cover tourists. Large hospitals often require payment upfront or guarantee of payment from your insurance. International clinics are popular with tourists. Keep all receipts for insurance reimbursement.

healthInfo.waterNotes: Tap water is safe to drink in South Korea. Bottled water is also widely available.
healthInfo.foodSafetyTips: Korean cuisine is generally very safe. Bibimbap, kimchi, bulgogi, and most Korean dishes are safe from restaurants. Raw fish (회) is popular — ensure it's from a reputable restaurant. Be cautious with very spicy food if you're not used to it. Food from street vendors (pojangmacha) is generally safe.
sources: South Korea Ministry of Food and Drug Safety
healthInfo.medicalTourismNote: South Korea is a major medical tourism destination, particularly for cosmetic surgery, dermatology, and advanced medical treatments. High quality at moderate costs.
